visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 accurately depicts the projectile launched from ground level with a parabolic path, coordinate axes, velocity vector/components, and vertical-motion equation, whereas Lesson 2 uses a generic/stylized trajectory and confusing zero-labeled vertical scale that does not faithfully represent the given 40 m/s, 30° projectile setup.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed, wired fill-in checkpoint after act_introduction with a real prompt, accepted answers, hint, and remediation path, while Lesson 2 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has clear, naturally paced narration with spoken math rendered appropriately, while Lesson 2 has no available narration transcript at all, making it absent on this dimension.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 provides timed visual cues that generally align with the narration’s references, while Lesson 2 has no transcript or cue timing available, so it cannot demonstrate any sync at all.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly decomposes the velocity, uses vertical motion to find flight time, and applies the range formula to get 141.4 m, while Lesson 2 has no available script or plan, so it provides no verifiable or learner-supporting conceptual explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 is much more visually polished with large legible typography, balanced full-frame compositions, and consistent cinematic styling, while Lesson 1’s mid-lesson diagram is tiny, pushed into the lower-left with excessive empty space, low-contrast/illegible labels, and a cluttered UI-like layout.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner: five of six dimension agents favored it with very high confidence, including visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and concept accuracy. These dimensions indicate that Lesson 1 is instructionally complete, mathematically correct, well narrated, synchronized, and includes functioning learner interaction. Lesson 2 was preferred only on polish, also with high confidence, due to stronger typography and visual composition, but this single advantage does not outweigh its lack of available narration, interactivity, conceptual explanation, synchronization evidence, and faithful projectile representation.
